title: One scarf. Too much ambition.
body:
Red scarf, last seen making a determined effort to leave the grounds on a gust of wind.

If it lands near you, please leave it with a prefect. This is a request for help, not permission to climb out of a tower window.

title: Quiet company wanted
body:
A few of us are putting together a quiet study group. Bring your own notes and something you can read without explaining every sentence aloud.

Companionable silence counts as participation.

title: The blue notebook
body:
If you borrowed the blue notebook full of river sketches, I would very much like it back.

If you borrowed it to find out whether the sketches matched the river, please dry it first. Curiosity is admirable. Soggy pages are less so.

title: A worthy opponent
body:
Looking for a chess partner among the older students. Patience and a willingness to lose gracefully would be appreciated.

I am working on the second requirement myself.

category: From the Head of Idris House
title: A name on the trunk, please
body:
A reminder to label your belongings clearly before asking the school brownies to help with them.

“It’s the trunk that looks like mine” is not a useful description. Neither, we are assured, is invisible ink.
signature: Professor Morwyn · Head of Idris House

title: The Howling Woods are still forbidden
body:
The Howling Woods remain out of bounds.

This includes when you are curious, when someone dares you, and when you are “only going to have a quick look.”

Please find a less exhausting way to test a prefect’s patience.

title: Please allow the post to land
body:
Red-kite deliveries are exciting enough without anyone waving breakfast overhead.

Please leave room for letters and parcels to arrive. A piece of toast is not a forwarding address.

title: A page or two in the courtyard
body:
If the weather holds, a few older students will be reading quietly in Founders’ Courtyard during our next free afternoon.

Bring a book and leave room for anyone who would like to sit. No one is obliged to discuss the ending.
signature: Carys Bowen · for the older students, all houses

title: A little consideration
body:
Please remember that the Central Hall is shared by everyone. Leave room for others to pass, collect your belongings and offer a hand when someone needs one.

A school is made welcoming by the people in it. I trust you to do your part.

title: A question is a good beginning
body:
If a passage in your history notes has left you uncertain, please bring it to our next lesson. You are welcome to ask me to explain it again.

Understanding takes time. There is no need to pretend that something is clear when it is not; we shall work through it together.

title: Brooms, balance and better judgement
body:
A reminder to older flying students: before braving brisk breezes, be certain your broom is in proper condition. Report battered bristles before they become a bothersome surprise.

Practise patient preparation, sensible speed and steady steering. Spectacular swooping is seldom a substitute for sound skill.

title: The scarf has come home
body:
Thank you to whoever left my scarf with a prefect. It is now safely back where it belongs.

If it asks anyone for directions to the towers, please remember that it has already had quite enough adventure.

title: Proper parking, please
body:
Please put practice brooms back in their proper places after flying.

A badly balanced broom becomes a bothersome barrier. Propping one across a passage is particularly poor planning.

Leave clear corridors for careful colleagues.

title: A name, a date, a little patience
body:
If the names and dates in your history notes have begun to blur together, try setting them out one small section at a time.

You need not untangle everything at once. Bring the parts that still puzzle you to our next lesson, and we shall look at them together.

title: Those are notes, not instructions
body:
To whoever borrowed my notebook: the arrows in the margins link one thought to another. They are not directions around the school.

I am sorry if the diagram brought you back to the same page three times. It did that to me as well.

category: From the Head of Idris House
title: Borrowed is not inherited
body:
Please return borrowed belongings when you have finished with them. This includes books, blankets and the chair you moved because it was “only for a moment.”

A polite request before borrowing is generally more successful than an elaborate explanation afterwards.
signature: Professor Morwyn · Head of Idris House

title: A little room on the page
body:
I have some spare parchment for the older students joining our study group. Please ask if you need a sheet.

If your notes have reached the point where the margins have margins, it may be time to start a fresh page.

title: Wind, weather and wise decisions
body:
Before flying, consider conditions carefully. Gusts are not games, and a brisk breeze is no invitation to boast.

Steady steering and sensible choices serve you better than spectacular stories about surviving something foolish.

title: A rematch, with fewer excuses
body:
Thank you to the older students who answered my request for chess partners. I have enjoyed the games, including the ones I am still trying to explain.

For the next round, I shall accept that the board is not biased. I would appreciate the same courtesy from anyone who loses to me.

title: Small kindnesses count
body:
Thank you to those who have helped a neighbour find a misplaced belonging, made room at a table or taken a moment to listen.

These things do not require an announcement. They do, however, deserve to be noticed. Please continue to make our school a welcoming place.

title: The long way is not compulsory
body:
If anyone among the older students would like company while we work through our notes, please come and ask.

You do not need to make a dramatic entrance. After the scarf incident, I am trying to show a little restraint.

title: You may change your mind
body:
Finding a mistake in your notes is not a reason to be discouraged. It means you have noticed something worth checking.

Cross it out, ask a question and give yourself time. Understanding is more important than appearing to have been right all along.

title: One glove, seeking its other half
body:
Found: one grey glove, apparently abandoned by its partner.

If it is yours, please ask a prefect to put you in touch with me. Describing it as “the grey one” will not narrow things down as much as you hope.
